## The group members (names and UNIs)

Giuliana Motta (gem2176), Jonathan Morris (jsm2298), Max Hyman (mjh2289), Emma Johnston (eej2124) 

## The tentative project title

311, What's Your Emergency? Pigeons. 

## The motivation for this project

As an avid New York City birder, I look through my binoculars each weekend. And what do I see? Pigeons. From a distance, these birds are, at most, a minor nuisance (as they scare away other birds). However, to many people, they are enough of a bother to submit pigeon-related complaints via 311. We were curious to investigate the issues these pigeons cause in the lives of New Yorkers. 

## The intended final products

We want to describe and analyze pigeon-related complaints in NYC using publicly available data from 311  Complaint Data that feature the word 'pigeon'. This will include static visualizations that characterize complaints by time, location, income level, and building type. Furthermore, we will identify the species of pigeons that are present in NYC using eBird. We also plan to create a dashboard that utilizes the API available via the data source to provide real-time pigeon complaint updates. Finally, we will analyze factors that may be associated with pigeon complaints and response time, including time, building type, location/borough, and socioeconomic factors, such as income.  

## The anticipated data sources

311 Pigeon Complaint Data: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Social-Services/contains-Pigeon-/iea7-sinw/about_data

eBird Observation Dataset (EOD): https://www.gbif.org/dataset/4fa7b334-ce0d-4e88-aaae-2e0c138d049e 

Census data (for income): https://www.census.gov/topics/income-poverty/income/data/tables.html 

## The planned analyses / visualizations / coding challenges

### Planned analyses: 

1) Temporal trend of complaints 

* 16 years of data - have the amount of complaints changed? 

* yearly and seasonal trends in the level of complaints 

2) Geographical distribution of complaints 

* By borough and neighborhood 

* temporal trends of pigeon complaints by borough 
  
3) Type and details of pigeon-related complaint 

* Problem: Unsanitary pigeon condition or trapping pigeon 

* Problem detail: Pigeon waste or pigeon odor 
        
4) Pigeon complaint by building type 

* mixed use apartment, residential building, school, street area 
    
5) Brief scientific overview of pigeon species in NYC 

6) Are there correlations between where pigeon sightings are reported on eBird and where people file pigeon complaints?

7) Use an API and have a dashboard of real-time pigeon reporting 

8) How long it takes for a 311 Pigeon call to get resolved

* could look at that by income 

### Visualizations: 

* Tables or bar charts for intended final projects (especially location type and borough)

* Chart showing temporal trends in pigeons 

* histogram of how long it takes to resolve a pigeon complaint. We could vary that by borough or income level 

* Map of pigeon sightings and map of pigeon complaints

### Potential coding challenges: 

* Amount of pigeon data available (we have 16 years of data, but realistically how many people are submitting pigeon complaints?)

* How the data is stratified within the datasets 

* Co-locating pigeon species data to New York City using longitude and latitude 

* Working with dates and timestamps for the complaints (when the complaints were opened and closed)

* Some of the complaints have not been closed, so we have NA data for a lot of complaint closures
